scope: Offline authored contract tests, not LLM evaluation, security certification, manufacturing or finance evidence
question: Can an existing workflow check whether an approval still binds to the current target, rule and declared evidence versions through a small adapter, and does RDF/SHACL provide a practical benefit over equivalent JSON rules?
motivation: Prior shared-semantics experiments already found matching decisions under matched JSON/RDF rules. This probe does not repeat that as a new ontology advantage. It isolates a possible reusable contract boundary.

graphs.data: Business entities and relations in source systems
graphs.evidence: Dependencies of a particular approval on versioned inputs; the only graph needed in this probe

candidate_interface.check: check(request, approval, dependencies, completeness) -> allow | deny | unknown, reason codes, actual checker execution
candidate_interface.impact: changed evidence IDs -> approvals with declared direct dependencies; shared infrastructure, not a SHACL advantage
candidate_interface.caller: An LLM or ordinary application may propose an action; a trusted host supplies current versions and enforces the result. This probe uses authored inputs and has no LLM.
candidate_interface.authority: A check is valid only for the supplied snapshot. It is not permission to execute later without snapshot/version rechecking. Authentication, atomic execution and provenance authenticity are outside this prototype.

arms: Independent Python rules over normalized JSON
RDF conversion plus actual pySHACL validation of equivalent bindings
shared: Same supplied versions and completeness assertion
comparison.fixtures: Twelve authored cases with separate expected statuses, including changed target/rule/dependency, missing input, revoked approval, duplicates and explicit empty dependency set. These are software examples, not independently sampled gold.
comparison.timing: Single local execution, descriptive only, no performance ranking
comparison.interpretation: Agreement establishes contract implementation consistency on these examples only. A SHACL failure is not proof the underlying source fact is false.

related_work.name: OPA agent tool calling
related_work.overlap: Already checks model tool requests, returns denial reasons, supports policy updates and decision logs. Tool-call checking itself is not a differentiator.

related_work.name: Cedar policy level validation
related_work.overlap: Restricts entity dereference depth and allows relevant entity slicing with equivalent decisions under those restrictions. Selecting only relevant relational context is not new by itself.

related_work.name: SHACL Validation under Graph Updates
related_work.overlap: Studies static preservation of constraints under update sequences for conforming graphs. It is not a direct runtime incremental-revalidation performance result for this prototype.

related_work.name: PROV-O
related_work.overlap: Existing vocabulary for provenance entities, activities and derivation; evidence dependencies are not a new ontology invention.

integration_costs: Map host object IDs and version tokens to normalized fields
Identify who owns current versions, approvals and completeness assertions
Record evidence dependencies when approving; absent dependencies cannot be recovered by SHACL
Translate or maintain policy definitions and review changes
Enforce snapshot/version consistency at actual execution

next_evidence_gate.before_new_library: Integrate the same contract in two existing workflows, record actual adapter edits and independently reviewed policy-change tasks. Compare against competent JSON/OPA implementations, not a missing-check baseline.
next_evidence_gate.promising: Same decisions with demonstrably easier audited cross-system rule reuse or clearer dependency explanations, without unacceptable conversion/setup cost
next_evidence_gate.negative: If binding and impact logic remain simpler as ordinary rules, publish fixtures/adapters or contribute to existing engines instead of building another platform.
next_evidence_gate.long_term: Ontology learning and selective module extraction remain separate future work. Automatically inferred dependencies cannot be trusted as complete without a separate validation protocol.

authorization: No paid model calls, databases, infrastructure, schedule changes or publication push in this probe
